note: Curated from the Btown Brief newsletter vault (editions Sep 11 - Oct 9, 2026, catching up a six-week backlog). TALKING-POINTS.md is the style doctrine; refreshes land as PRs and points age out via 'added'.

points.text: Burlington's WJOY just celebrated 80 years on the air, broadcasting on the AM dial since 1946 while most AM stations around it switched to talk or religious programming. What station would you still turn the dial to find?

Nineteen-year-old Mustafa Khudaier reopened the kiosk at Church and College as Sabah's House this summer, running his mother Sabah Abbas's family shawarma recipes after the family arrived in Vermont as refugees from Iraq twelve years ago. What's on your order the next time you're downtown?

The Vermont Historical Society just took in Big Heavy World's entire music archive, physical relics included — the ladle from Nectar's and the actual door from 242 Main are both part of the collection now. Which Burlington venue relic would you want preserved like that?

The Winooski Valley Park District paid $960,000 for Charlie's Boathouse at the end of North Avenue, kayaks and historic photos included, and it'll reopen as a public park next spring after decades as a family-run bait shop and boat rental. What do you picture doing there once it opens?

The old downtown YMCA is becoming 79 apartments, and crews are keeping the 1925 stone floor that local masons laid from Shelburne and Redstone quarry stone. Studio or four-bedroom — which unit would you pick once it opens next spring?

When the Greater Burlington YMCA accidentally locked everyone out one Saturday morning, instructor Wendy Ross-Atwood just moved her Strength and Burn class onto the sidewalk and led all 17 people through the workout anyway, music blasting from her husband's Tesla. Which workout would you be willing to do out on the sidewalk?
Breeze Airways just launched Burlington's first nonstop flight to Baltimore in 16 years, with fares advertised as low as $49. Where's the next cheap nonstop you'd want the airport to add?

The Princeton Review just named UVM the most LGBTQ-friendly college in the country, with the school saying 42% of this year's incoming class doesn't identify as straight or cisgender. Where would your own college have landed on that same list?

Bowl & Roll just opened on St. Paul Street with poke bowls, fire-grilled rice bowls and kati roll wraps, from a chef who moved from California just to open it with an old friend. What's the first bowl you're building?

Winooski just finished a $28.3 million rebuild of nearly 4,000 feet of Main Street — new bike lanes, buried utility lines, more than 200 new trees — a decade in the making. What's the first thing you'll notice walking down the new street?

UVM just landed a record $38 million federal grant to build an AI 'twin' of critically ill patients so doctors can test treatments on the model first. What's the first thing you'd want your own AI twin to test for you?

After October 17th, Haymaker's Soda Plant café closes to the public and turns into a full-time bakery shipping its frozen sticky bun four-packs nationwide. What's the Vermont snack you'd want to see on shelves everywhere?

Phish fans who started the Mockingbird Foundation back in 1996 just teamed up with VSAC to launch a new scholarship for Vermont music students. What show or album got you into music in the first place?

Chapin Orchard in Essex Junction counts on about eight good weekends to make its whole pick-your-own season work, and this year's crop held up fine despite an April frost. Which apple are you filling your bag with first?

Burlington High's Class of 1966 — only the second class to ever graduate from the old North Avenue building — came back this fall to tour the brand new BHS, and one alum was just glad to see the hill is still there for cross country meets. What's the one landmark from your old school you'd want to see again?

A visitor from Edmonton just set a new Darn Tough record, wearing one pair of the Waterbury company's wool socks for 101 days straight without washing them, smashing the old mark of 55. How many days do you think you could go?

VTrans has to offer up old bridges for free before tearing them down, so the 1928 span over the Winooski River is now listed on Vermont Craigslist — so far the only reply asked if they could move it tomorrow. What would you do with your own free bridge?

Scientists in White River Junction are gluing solar-powered trackers onto monarch butterflies and naming them things like Ann, Scott and Pam, and the data's already showing some winter in Florida instead of Mexico. What name would you give the next butterfly they tag?

Burlington High's new football field hosted its first game last month, and play stopped for ten minutes while they searched the parking lot for whoever was shining a laser pointer onto the field. What's the strangest reason you've seen a game get held up?

South Burlington's Cathy Seward just picked up a $10,000 Patriots Foundation award for King Street Center, seventeen years after she started there as a volunteer book buddy. What cause would you still be showing up for after seventeen years?

Burlington's Intervale Center just marked 20 years under director Travis Marcotte, who's helped nearly 1,000 Vermont farms get going, including one that now grows 350 to 400 pounds of mushrooms a week. What's the strangest thing you'd want to try growing yourself?
Burlington's weekly Ronald McDonald House bingo night just marked 40 years running, raising more than $2 million along the way under the same caller since 1986. What's your go-to bingo dauber color?
